BiblicalUsage: This word is used once, for the bright iron in the market of Tyre. Dan and Javan go to and fro in her fairs, and bright iron, cassia and calamus are in her market, among the goods the nations bring to the great city of the sea.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for polished iron carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that Tyre's wealth is made of bright metal and sweet spice, and it will all sink with her.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
